To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the resting-state functional connectivity in the left posterior superior-temporal cortex increases with age and is positively associated with language performance in children with greater advancement of sentence comprehension abilities.
the changes in neural network connectivity in the left posterior STG and the left inferior frontal cortex are related to the developmental trajectory of language abilities in young children.

the neural connectivity in a cluster within left posterior superior temporal sulcus/gyrus (STS/STG) increased with age in preschool children and that this increase was positively related to language performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the language network and its functional connectivity in children with typical language development.
the development of language and its neural correlates in children.
the neural basis of sentence comprehension in children.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the changes in functional connectivity in the left STG/STS are not only related to age per se, but also in a more direct way to language performance, which suggests that the changes in this region are specifically related to language development.

the developmental increase of RSFC between the posterior left STG and other regions of language network, i. e. left and right IFG, is positively correlated with the improvement of sentence comprehension ability in the preschool children.
the present findings suggest a developmental trajectory for the language network, which is in line with previous reports of a maturing language network in children.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the changes in language network are not just a function of age but are also related to language performance.
the development of language in young children is associated with the development of the functional connectivity of the language network.
the changes in functional connectivity in language areas during early childhood are correlated with the improvement of language abilities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development of the language network can be tracked with resting state fMRI, and that this can provide a powerful tool to study language development in children with language impairments.
the development of language is associated with the maturation of the language network.
the neural connectivity changes in the left posterior STG and STS during the transition from 5 to 6 years of age are related to language development.
